author: Mike Lacett
title: How the Greens get so green at Quail Hollow Club in Charlotte - NewsBreak
text:
By Mike Lacett ,
1 hours ago
CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( CAROLINA SPORTS LIVE ) — Time is running out at Quail Hollow Club.
“We call this advance week,” Director of Greens & Grounds Keith Wood explains. “It’s the week before the event.”
And much like those well-known workers in the North Pole, right before Christmas…
“It’s like Santa Claus and his elves,” he says.
Wood and his 42-member grounds crew aren’t getting much sleep.
“It’s daylight to dark now,” he says.
He pauses, then adds, “It’s so fantastic.”
It’s a good thing they enjoy the work. Then again, it’s an even better thing that they’re darn good at it. After all, the battle against Mother Nature and 165 acres of grass isn’t easy.
“The team has great pride in what they do,” Wood says. “They want to put out a good product.”
And more often than not, they do.
It’s no accident that the greens at Quail are always so green. These guys have it down to a science.
“We plan out our agronomic schedules. Based on the weather patterns, we know when the grass is going to look its best.”
The term Wood uses is peaking the golf course. He says Quail Hollow looks great 357 days a year. But that one week, tournament week, it has to look extra special.
“The greenkeepers do a heck of a job. When people see it on TV or when people come out and experience it on site, we want them to be awed and say, ‘Wow,'” Wood says.
It’s perhaps the most important part of the fan experience at Truist Championship.
“Yeah, there is so much more pressure,” he admits.
But if it’s done right…
“For me, it’s sunrise on round four. All the hard work is done,” he says.
It can feel like winning it all.
